title: Austria's Foreign Ministry reports unauthorized access via an external provider's website
date_note: Date of the ministry communiqué as relayed by N+ (Friday, 20 November); the access is reported as 12 to 13 November.
geo_basis: agency headquarters (Vienna, as the article refers to staff in Vienna)
summary: N+ reports that Austria's Foreign Ministry said in a communiqué that unauthorized access occurred on 12 and 13 November through a website run by an external service provider. Per N+, it was detected on 13 November and blocked immediately. N+ says names and professional contact details of staff were exposed, and that an analysis ruled out exposure of workers' personal data. No attacker is named.
plain: Austria's Foreign Ministry reportedly said someone got into a website run by an outside provider on 12 and 13 November. It was blocked once found.
exec: A government ministry reports an intrusion through a supplier's website; supplier-hosted sites can be a way into organisations.
impact: Per N+: names and professional contact details of staff in Vienna and at missions abroad; personal data ruled out as exposed.

validation.note: Only N+ read; the ministry's own communiqué was not found or read. N+ distinguishes professional contact details (exposed) from workers' personal data (ruled out).

review.note: Checked against N+ (20 Nov): dates, detection, external provider site match. Summary wrongly called the article inconsistent; N+ says professional contact details exposed and personal data ruled out. Rewrote summary, impact, validation note; no attacker named.
